metadata.title: Screens the Deal. Doesn't Decide It.
metadata.subtitle: The Deal-Screening Skill (Financial Services)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to screen a deal, is it deciding whether the fund should pursue it, or running a fixed spec on what you give it? Lands the carry-out that deal-screening doesn't author the decision — it runs the SKILL.md's pass/fail checks on your inputs and hands you a memo, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed deal-screening would decide whether the fund should do this deal. It doesn't — it screens the materials against your criteria. Does deal-screening screen this deal for me?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is deal-screening. Its SKILL.md holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads the file, then acts on it. The file is the program.
The instructions live in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — linear, one after another, unless a step itself says to branch.

production_viz.label: ONE STEP AT A TIME
production_viz.caption: no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: deal-screening's job is specific: extract the deal's key metrics, run them through a pass/fail framework against the fund's investment criteria, and output a one-page screening memo. What isn't in the SKILL.md's steps isn't part of the job.
deal-screening doesn't decide if you should do the deal — it runs the SKILL.md's pass/fail checks against your criteria and hands you a memo, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Paste this into Claude: 'I want to quickly screen inbound deal flow — CIMs, teasers, and broker materials — against my fund's investment criteria. Read the deal-screening skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it.' That last clause matters — asking Claude to explain first surfaces the actual steps it's about to run.
